sentences.en: Good evening, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: Today, we are delighted to have invited Jim Johnson, a gapyear.com’s spokesperson, to talk about gap year.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们很高兴邀请到gapyear.com网站的发言人吉姆·约翰逊，来谈谈间隔年。

sentences.en: So, whether you’re currently deciding whether a gap year is for you, or you’re just feeling itchy to decide what to do with it, you are welcome to join us. Well, Jim.
sentences.zh: 无论你正在考虑自己是否适合间隔年，还是已经迫不及待地想决定如何度过间隔年，都欢迎加入我们。那么，吉姆。

w.m: adj. 跃跃欲试的；急切的

sentences.en: Thanks. I am very pleased to meet you all.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。很高兴见到大家。

sentences.en: Now, let me first ask you a question. Why should young people be thinking seriously about taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 我先问您一个问题。为什么年轻人应该认真考虑过一个间隔年呢？

sentences.en: Well, I get asked this question all the time.
sentences.zh: 我一直都会被问到这个问题。

sentences.en: People will tell you that a gap year boosts your CV, that it makes you more employable, or that it even prepares you for a life at university.
sentences.zh: 别人会告诉你，间隔年能为简历加分，让你更容易就业，甚至能帮助你为大学生活做好准备。

sentences.en: Well, this is the case, but I find not enough people put an emphasis on just how amazing a gap year really is.
sentences.zh: 这些话确实没错，但我发现，还没有足够多的人强调间隔年本身有多么精彩。

sentences.en: Eh, it’s a life changing experience, and it’s unbelievable how much fun you can have on a gap year.
sentences.zh: 它能改变人生，而你在间隔年里获得的乐趣之多，也会令人难以置信。

sentences.en: So, what is the best thing about taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 那么，间隔年最大的好处是什么呢？

sentences.en: I think taking a gap year is like making a journey.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，间隔年就像开启一段旅程。

sentences.en: It’s an education, an exploration and an adventure.
sentences.zh: 它是一次学习、一次探索，也是一场冒险。

sentences.en: You learn so much about exotic cultures and traditions, their culinary art, their political system, their religion.
sentences.zh: 你能深入了解异国文化与传统，以及那里的烹饪艺术、政治制度和宗教。

sentences.en: In each new location, you’re learning more and more, and that ultimately adds more value to yourself, which is the best thing, I think.
sentences.zh: 每到一个新地方，你都会学到越来越多东西，最终让自身更有价值；我觉得，这才是最棒的。

sentences.en: What did your gap year involve?
sentences.zh: 您的间隔年都做了些什么？

sentences.en: I travelled for two years through Central Asia, Southeast Asia and Australia, you know, backpacking, volunteering and moonlighting abroad.
sentences.zh: 我用了两年时间游历中亚、东南亚和澳大利亚，在国外背包旅行、做志愿服务，也打些零工。

sentences.en: So I had a pretty comprehensive gap.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的间隔年经历相当丰富。

sentences.en: To put it simple, it was the best two years in my life.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，那是我人生中最美好的两年。

w.m: 表达. 简单来说（规范表达为to put it simply）

sentences.en: It can be difficult to decide what to do and where to go on your gap year, so what advice would you have for people finding it tricky?
sentences.zh: 决定间隔年做什么、去哪里，可能很困难；对于为此感到棘手的人，您有什么建议？

sentences.en: Good question. The most important thing is research and planning.
sentences.zh: 问得好。最重要的是调研和规划。

sentences.en: That is, sit down with a map and a sheet of paper.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，拿张地图和一张纸，坐下来好好想想。

sentences.en: List where you want to go and why.
sentences.zh: 列出你想去哪里，以及为什么想去。

sentences.en: Maybe even throw in a pros and cons column.
sentences.zh: 甚至还可以加上一栏，写下利弊。

sentences.en: Others may advise talking to friends with some experience of gap year, or browse some online forums, which I personally would not highly recommend.
sentences.zh: 有人可能建议找有间隔年经验的朋友聊聊，或浏览网上论坛；我个人并不特别推荐这些做法。

sentences.en: Don’t choose what is the best out there, but what is most appropriate for you.
sentences.zh: 不要选择外界公认最好的，而要选择最适合自己的。

sentences.en: OK, let’s move on to another question.
sentences.zh: 好，我们接着谈另一个问题。

sentences.en: Which project would you do if you were taking a gap year?
sentences.zh: 如果您要过一个间隔年，您会选择哪个项目？

sentences.en: I’m a bit of a diving nut, so I would go for the Madagascar Marine Conservation and Diving Project.
sentences.zh: 我是个潜水迷，所以会选择马达加斯加海洋保护与潜水项目。

sentences.en: It’s got everything you want.
sentences.zh: 你想要的，它都具备。

sentences.en: It’s relatively cheap, especially when you consider what you’re getting, and you get to learn all about marine conservation.
sentences.zh: 它的费用相对便宜，尤其考虑到你能获得的收获；你还能全面学习海洋保护知识。

sentences.en: Oh, and it’s in Madagascar, one of the best places to go diving in the world.
sentences.zh: 而且，项目在马达加斯加，那可是世界上最适合潜水的地方之一。

sentences.en: Do employers or universities care what you’ve done on your gap year?
sentences.zh: 雇主或大学会在意你在间隔年里做过什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes, they really do. If you’re studying veterinary science and you volunteer on a wildlife conservation project, then that can really boost your CV and experience levels by doing so.
sentences.zh: 会的，他们确实很在意。如果你学兽医学，又参加了野生动物保护项目的志愿工作，这样的经历就能实实在在地为简历加分、丰富你的经验。

sentences.en: Recently, at gapyear.com, we conducted a survey asking HR professionals whether a gap year makes a job applicant more employable. 63% agreed that a constructive gap year, either just a few months or a year sharp spent volunteering or gaining work experience overseas, makes a job application stand out, so the evidence is there.
sentences.zh: 最近，gapyear.com对人力资源专业人士开展了一项调查，询问间隔年是否会让求职者更具就业竞争力。63%的受访者表示，一段有意义的间隔年经历，无论是几个月还是一年，用来参加志愿活动或积累海外工作经验，都能使求职申请脱颖而出；这就是依据。

w.m: adj. 有益的；有建设性的
